morph.note: Past active participle in -वत् (ktavatu) of √वच्, with samprasāraṇa (वच् → उक्-): उक्तवत् ‘having said’. In narrative it does the work of a finite past verb: ‘(they) said’. Dual, for the two asuras.
The suffix -तस् added to a pronoun stem gives an ablative adverb: अस्मत्तः ‘from us’, त्वत्तः ‘from you’ (1.62).
Passive imperative of √वृ ‘to choose’: the root becomes व्रि- before the passive -य-. ‘Let a boon be chosen from us’ is the courteous form of ‘choose a boon’.

mantras.anvaya_en: The subject तौ is in 1.94; the quoted words are closed by इति, and केशवम् is the person addressed.
mantras.lit: said to Keśava: ‘Let a boon be chosen from us.’
mantras.tr: said to Keśava, “Choose a boon from us.”
mantras.tr_note: The passive ‘let a boon be chosen’ is rendered as an active imperative.

comm.t: The delusion shows itself as pride: after five thousand years of combat the asuras, pleased with their opponent, offer him a boon — as though they were the gods and he the petitioner.
The reversal is the point the tradition draws: a boon is a superior’s gift. In offering one to Viṣṇu the asuras act out the confusion that Mahāmāyā has worked in them (1.94).

comm.t: Viṣṇu answers the asuras’ offer. Inside Medhas’s narration the text quotes the god directly, under the same label the Bhagavad Gītā uses for Kṛṣṇa’s speeches.

sandhi.type: no change (final m before a vowel)
sandhi.rule: final m joins a following vowel
sandhi.note: Final m before a vowel is written with it, not as anusvāra.
Final au before a vowel becomes āv, twice: वध्यौ + उभौ → वध्यावुभौ; उभौ + अपि → उभावपि.

morph.note: Optative third-person dual. The subject is the pronominal adjective उभौ ‘both’, so the verb is third person even though Viṣṇu is speaking to the two asuras (‘may both (of you) be …’); an understood भवन्तौ ‘your honours’ would give the same person. The optative expresses a wish that is also a demand: it is the boon he names.
Gerundive ‘to be killed, fit to be killed’, from वध, the form √हन् takes in several derivatives. With a gerundive the agent may stand in the genitive: मम वध्यौ ‘to be killed by me’.
Past participle of √तुष् in an active sense (‘satisfied’), with the genitive मे ‘with me’. It states the condition the asuras themselves have just declared.

mantras.anvaya: (यतः युवाम्) अद्य मे तुष्टौ, (अतः) उभौ अपि मम वध्यौ भवेताम्।
mantras.anvaya_en: A single optative clause; तुष्टौ is circumstantial (‘since you are pleased’), and the anvaya spells out the implied condition. Alternatively भवेताम् can be supplied twice: ‘may you be pleased with me; may you both be slain by me’.
mantras.lit: (Since you are) pleased with me today, may you both be (persons) to be slain by me.
mantras.tr: If you are pleased with me, then let both of you be slain by me today.
mantras.tr_note: The participle तुष्टौ is rendered as a condition (‘if you are pleased’); the Sanskrit states it without a conjunction.

comm.t: Viṣṇu accepts the offer and asks the one thing that ends the war: that both asuras be killable by him. Their own boon becomes the instrument of their death.

The motif of a boon turned against the giver recurs in the Purāṇas. Here it carries the chapter’s teaching: the asuras are undone not by Viṣṇu’s strength, which five thousand years did not make decisive, but by the delusion of Mahāmāyā.

sandhi_exceptions.reason: The vowels stand apart at the pāda break (वरेणात्र | एतावद्धि): epic verse often leaves sandhi unapplied between the first and second pādas, and joining (अत्रैतावत्) would take a syllable from the line. A metrical licence, printed so in the Gita Press text.

sandhi.note: a + e should give ai (अत्रैतावत्); the text leaves the vowels apart at the pāda break. Declared in sandhi_exceptions.
Final t becomes d before the voiced h, and the h then takes the aspiration of the stop: d + h → ddh.

morph.note: किम् with an instrumental of the thing is an idiom for ‘what is the use of …?’: किम् अन्येन वरेण ‘what (good is) another boon?’
Past participle of √वृ ‘to choose’ (वृ + त), neuter to agree with एतावत्. With the genitive मम it reads ‘chosen by me’ or simply ‘my choice’.

mantras.anvaya: अत्र अन्येन वरेण किम्? एतावत् हि मम वृतम्।
mantras.anvaya_en: A rhetorical question and a statement; हि gives the reason (‘for this much is my choice’).
mantras.lit: What (use is there) here of another boon? For this much (is) chosen by me.
mantras.tr: What need have I of any other boon? This alone is my choice.

comm.t: Viṣṇu closes off any bargaining: he wants nothing else. The asuras, bound by their offer, cannot refuse.
The hiatus अत्र | एतावत् falls at the pāda break and is printed so in the Gita Press text; it is a licence of epic verse, not an error, and is kept.

comm.t: Medhas takes up the narrative again after Viṣṇu’s two lines (1.97–98) and tells how the asuras tried to escape the boon they had granted.
